items.excerpt:
A dashboard shows a temperature spike. That number came from somewhere. An API picked it up. A service moved it along. A query pulled it out of storage.
One weak spot anywhere in that chain and the reading can lie. The tools in this article look at the software that builds those chains. Not the cables. Not the switches. Not the machines themselves.
Five platforms, all aimed at teams writing factory apps, cloud services, and the dashboards people watch on the floor.
Two topics sit outside what follows. Watching a control network. Certifying a safety function. Those need their own tools.
The software running a factory floor gets written by people, not machines. Aikido was put together for those people. Robots and assembly lines used to run on hardware alone. These days the code carries just as much of the load.
Spotting a flaw is the easy half. The hard half is getting it closed.
Three separate scans normally mean three separate queues. Aikido pulls them onto one screen. What floats to the top follows context, not raw severity. Four people do not have time for a hundred warnings. They have time for the few that could genuinely bite.
Noise falls by up to 85%. From there, an AI step takes each real hit and pushes it toward a patch, so nobody faces a blank page.
Setup barely registers. Nothing installed on any machine. Nothing to maintain. The whole thing talks over an API. GDPR and ISO 27001 checks arrive built in, which saves a step for anyone working under a regulator.
Source. Libraries. Images. One screen, one queue, and a person who knows what happens next.
Snyk got its start on the outside parts. Imported packages. Pulled-in libraries. That is still where it shines. Later it added the code your team writes and the images you deploy. Extensions exist for editors, repositories, and build servers.
Now think about a typical factory project. A dashboard pulls in a charting library. An API rests on a web framework. A worker pulls a queue client and a database driver. None of those were written in-house. All of them came from somewhere else.
That is the problem. Every import is a possible hole. Snyk walks the pile. Matches each package against published CVE lists. Then drops the suggested patch right beside the line that needs it, in the editor the developer already has open.
Image scanning rides along. A service packaged for a plant machine gets checked the same way as the code stuffed inside it.

items.description: The movement of a robot arm occurs after a signal is sent out by the controller. But there is another world beyond the controller. There are Python services that queue up tasks. items.excerpt:
The movement of a robot arm occurs after a signal is sent out by the controller. But there is another world beyond the controller.
There are Python services that queue up tasks. There are Java backends responding to API requests. Modules are passing around data.
Bugs live there too. A weak validator within an API handler. A common login component that takes faulty input. It all stays away from hardware. It all has the potential to halt the assembly line if a mistake gets by.
SAST reads code the way a proofreader reads a draft. Nothing runs yet. The flaws show up on the page.
What follows covers five tools built for Python and Java backends. Where each one digs. How deep it goes across files. Where it fits in a normal working day.
One boundary before we start. Firmware security sits elsewhere. So does functional-safety certification. Neither belongs in this comparison.
Choose the wrong scanner and the team will spend months babysitting it. But what is really important here?
Language first. If the backend runs Python and Java, the tool has to handle both. Not every scanner does. Some treat one as an afterthought.
Then the part most people miss. A vulnerability rarely sits in one file.
Picture the path. A request hits an API handler. It moves through a validation function. It lands in a database query written in a completely different module.
A scanner that reads each file alone sees three innocent pieces. Nothing connects them. Cross-file analysis connects them.
Integration decides whether findings ever get fixed. A warning buried in a separate security dashboard tends to sit there. A warning posted as a comment on the pull request gets answered.
And the usual suspects deserve attention. Injection flaws. Broken authentication. Insecure deserialization. Hardcoded secrets left in a config file. These show up in automation backends as often as anywhere else.
The tools below differ in analysis depth, language support, and how they fit into development workflows. Each has a place, depending on team size and existing processes.

Industrial software incorporates existing libraries and external dependencies to streamline development. These components power manufacturing applications, industrial control systems, and other solutions.
However, you might need to address security weaknesses and licensing violations in industrial systems. Traditional security testing can’t fully cover every component. SCA tools will help you address this gap.
We gathered some of the best SCA tools in this article to help you find a solution that will match your security requirements. So, keep reading!
SCA is a security practice that identifies and evaluates open-source components and dependencies within your software application.
It’s pretty difficult to track thousands of external libraries manually. SCA tools automate this process. They help your development and security teams understand which components they use and what risks they may introduce.
One of the main functions of SCA is dependency discovery. These tools identify software components and their versions by scanning
So, you can detect direct dependencies added to a project and any transitive dependencies.
SCA tools also check identified components against vulnerability databases. They can report the severity of each vulnerability and help you assess the potential impact. Some solutions also recommend safer versions and alternative components.
Open-source license compliance is another important capability of these tools. These licenses outline specific rules for software use and distribution. SCA tools help you identify them and enforce internal policies.
Many SCA platforms also generate and manage an SBOM. They help you track dependencies and manage any new vulnerabilities. Plus, they provide customers and auditors with information about your software supply chain.
Not to mention that these tools can help you with your remediation efforts. They let you focus on components that are exposed to potential attacks or affect critical systems. It’s useful in industrial environments, where software updates require extensive testing and scheduled maintenance.

items.excerpt:
Renewables made up 85.6% of all new power capacity added worldwide in 2025, according to the International Renewable Energy Agency’s Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026.
Each new solar park, wind farm, and battery site adds another stream of operational data. Energy companies turn those streams into value through data platforms built for different jobs.
The hard part starts before the first vendor call. Without a clear list of sources, owners, and constraints, vendors fill the gaps with assumptions, and proposals for one project arrive with different scopes and prices.
This article reviews the best firms providing energy data platform development services and the work each one has delivered. You will also find what to prepare before you brief a vendor, from a data source inventory to security limits, and how to test your chosen vendor through a pilot before a full build.
A vendor can only price and plan what you describe. Here are the 6 inputs that give every shortlisted firm the same starting point and make their proposals comparable:
List every system that produces data the platform will use: SCADA historians, meter head-ends, IoT gateways, asset registers, weather services, and market feeds.
For each source, note the format, how often it updates, the time zone it logs in, and roughly how much data it produces a day.
Vendors size ingestion and storage from this list, so a missing source shows up later as a change request. A spreadsheet with one row per source is enough to start your brief.
Every source needs a named owner who can approve access and answer questions about the data. Write down who that person is, which team they sit in, and how a vendor would get read access, whether through an API, a database replica, or file exports.
Access requests for control systems can take weeks, so starting them before the brief keeps your project schedule intact.
A week of real data from each main source shows a vendor what written descriptions miss. Anonymize customer details if needed, but keep the original timestamps, units, and gaps. Vendors use these samples to spot quality problems early and to estimate the cleaning work in your proposal.
State where the data may live: a specific cloud, your own data center, or a hybrid setup. Add the standards your security team applies, such as ISO 27001 or NERC CIP, and any rule that keeps control-system networks closed to inbound traffic.

items.excerpt:
How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering
Meta 工程团队详解如何把 AI 智能体作为开发流程参与者来构建独立 Groups 应用 Forum，采用 human-on-the-loop 模式并以验证通过的生产级产出衡量成功。Forum 在八周内达到与 Facebook Groups 的核心功能对齐，自主压测循环在开发期发现并修复了内存问题，内存占用和缺页约减半，上线后智能体还协助根因分析用户反馈。
原文复盘了 Meta 以智能体参与开发全流程的具体做法与度量标准，可迁移的工程经验比较扎实。
Forum 是一款独立的小组应用，由一个小团队从零开始构建。它也是我们测试一种不同工作方式的场所：将 AI 智能体视为工程流程的参与者，而不是更快的打字方式。
这项实验需要定义成功，而我们的标准不是代码量。我们衡量的是经过验证、可投入生产的结果——能够构建、通过测试并经受审查的变更。
仅将 AI 指向编码步骤本身并不会带来太大改变。当我们将这一方法扩展到实现前后的各个阶段——规划、构建、测试和验证——我们的成果开始复利式增长。看清这一转变最直观的方式，是看每个步骤由谁主导。
在 human-in-the-loop 模式下，工程师驱动每一步，AI 在其中辅助，自动补全函数、建议修复方案或回答问题。 每次迭代都以驱动者本人的节奏推进。
在 human-on-the-loop 模式下，智能体自行运行迭代——规划、实现、构建、测试、修正、重复——而工程师设定目标、观察运行、在偏离时介入并批准结果。人的工作从执行步骤转变为对结果负责并守住质量标准。这是我们努力的方向，而非已完成的终态：如今有些阶段已能自主运行，而另一些阶段仍需工程师参与每次迭代。
当工程师进行监督时，工作不再是严格的顺序执行。过去一次只能运行一个的循环可以重叠，工程师的时间用于方向和判断，而不是坐在循环里等待。但这一切只有在返回的结果可信时才成立。没有验证，AI 生成的代码会带来一个熟悉的问题——看似合理但无人确认其真正可用的输出，工程师随后不得不阅读、调试，并常常将其丢弃。弱信号并不能消除这一约束；它们只是把约束从编写代码转移到审查那些看起来已完成、实则不然的代码上。
因此我们把标准设在验证而非编译上。编译不是终点——只有自动化测试和视觉检查都通过，任务才算完成。智能体在工程师看到之前先检查自己的工作，这意味着到达审查环节的是一组数量更少、可信度更高的结果，而不是一堆需要筛选的输出。生成得更少，丢弃的也更少。每个交付的结果仍需工程师签字确认；我们的努力在于让这一签字确认快速且有据可依，将构建结果、测试结果和录制的验证会话附加到变更上。
将规划作为技术规范： 智能体执行需要极高的精确度。工程师可能凭直觉解决的歧义会导致智能体失败。我们投入于严格的上游分解和机器可读的上下文，这为工程师和智能体同样收紧了工程闭环。
循环内的自动化验证是力量倍增器： 我们将自动化的通过/失败信号——构建状态、单元测试和 UI 规范匹配——直接集成到智能体循环中。这使得异步开发能够产出可供审查的拉取请求，并预先填充测试计划和录制的验证会话。验证是最难做对的部分，而我们能安全地交给循环多少，取决于我们能多大程度信任验证器。
使用智能体进行模拟用户测试： 我们部署了导航智能体，它们像真人一样与实时应用交互。这些智能体执行操作、读取屏幕并报告回归问题。导航智能体能够持续运行相同的验证路径。
智能体化生产运维： 发布后，智能体帮助自动化根因分析。当使用 Forum 的人提交反馈时，智能体会利用该反馈调查可能的回归问题。随后智能体将分析转发给工程师，由工程师决定下一步行动。
架构清晰性优先于继承的复杂性： 我们努力保持 Forum 的代码库尽可能简单直接，并选择将架构的关键部分模块化，以便在获得久经考验的基础设施优势的同时，也让智能体能够轻松即插即用。在无法轻易做到的地方，我们从头重建，以复用性换取智能体吞吐量，事实证明这在开发速度上很有回报。智能体从它们阅读的代码中学习模式。修复一次薄弱的模式，未来每个智能体会话都会继承这一改进；放任不管，同样的捷径就会出现在智能体接下来编写的所有内容中。
给智能体工具，而不是描述： 我们的主要失败模式是智能体搞不清自己在应用中的位置——让它修改群组主页时却去编辑首页信息流，或者靠猜屏幕坐标。所以，我们没有向智能体描述应用，而是给它工具去核查：从模拟器读取实时视图层级、列出屏幕上实际存在的元素、查找通往目标视图的路径——全部在它行动之前完成。误操作的编辑大幅减少。我们在智能体接触系统的所有地方都采用了同样的方法：给智能体一种直接核查状态的方式，而不是让它基于描述去推理。
为安全的 AI 原型开发提供构建级隔离： 随着 Forum 逐步走向生产环境，我们希望早期原型和智能体生成的实验有运行空间，同时让生产应用严格只包含已完成、经过审查的工作。我们想要比单纯的功能开关更强的保证——功能开关下原型代码仍然存在于生产构建中。我们的解决方案是一个 独立的构建变体 ，一个沙盒应用，它与生产环境共享完全相同的代码库、框架和设计系统，但通过插件/套接字架构将原型代码完全 排除 在生产构建之外。
改造环境不仅让智能体构建起来更快——它还让智能体成了测试员。我们没有把它指向某个具体缺陷。相反，我们设置了可重复的压力场景来模拟真实用户行为（激进滚动、随机浏览群组、快速导航、反复加载媒体），并在各构建中例行运行。由于这些运行会产生一致的信号（崩溃、内存增长、页面错误、UI 回归），智能体可以分诊异常、缩小到触发序列，然后调查根本原因。
其中一次运行暴露了一个内存问题。智能体隔离出复现步骤、提出修复方案并验证了它——全部在开发期间完成，早于应用到达用户手中。该修复在反复的压力会话中显著减少了设备上的内存增长和页面错误。
虽然架构决策由工程师做出，但检测和回归监控是自动化且可重复的；一旦检测到异常，智能体就能用同一套测试框架完成复现

items.excerpt:
Virtual data rooms are designed for business processes where confidential documents must be shared with multiple internal and external parties under controlled access.
M&A due diligence is the best-known example, but VDRs are also used for fundraising, audits, restructuring, real estate transactions, and other document-heavy projects.
This review looks at the Ideals virtual data room from a practical buyer’s perspective: what the platform offers, how its pricing is structured, and which workflows it is designed to support.
The aim is not to label one platform universally superior, but to identify the factors organizations should verify against their own requirements.
The Ideals data room combines document management, access control, reporting, Q&A, and security settings in a single project environment.
Administrators can organize participants into groups and assign permissions according to the information each group should be able to access.
According to the current Ideals Help Center, the platform provides eight document permission levels. Permissions are assigned at the group level, can be applied to folders and supported files, and can be changed during the project.
This structure is useful when bidders, advisers, specialists, and internal teams require different views of the same data room.
Document organization is central to a VDR because security alone does not make a review efficient. Ideals supports folder-based organization, document access controls, search, reporting, and other tools intended to help participants work through large document sets.
Administrators can also use project security settings such as two-step verification and restrictions based on IP addresses or domains. These controls are especially relevant when a project includes external users working from different organizations or locations.
The access model is consistent with the NIST principle of least privilege , which recommends restricting users to the minimum access necessary to perform assigned tasks. Buyers should still test the actual permission configuration they plan to use rather than relying only on a feature list.
For due diligence, document access is only part of the workflow. Reviewers also need a controlled way to ask questions, while administrators need visibility into project activity.

items.title: Closing the Loop: How Automated Plants Turn Wastewater into Process Water
items.description: Water is the utility most automation projects overlook. A plant that has instrumented every conveyor, robot cell and packaging line still sends its rinse water, cooling tower blowdown and process effluent to drain, then buys fresh water to replace it. Industrial water reuse changes that. Treated effluent comes back as cooling tower makeup, washdown water […]
items.excerpt:
Water is the utility most automation projects overlook. A plant that has instrumented every conveyor, robot cell and packaging line still sends its rinse water, cooling tower blowdown and process effluent to drain, then buys fresh water to replace it.
Industrial water reuse changes that. Treated effluent comes back as cooling tower makeup, washdown water or process feed, and the same control architecture that runs the production line keeps the water loop within specification.
Reuse projects fail when a system is sized from a brochure instead of from the plant’s own water. Rinse water from a metal finishing line, effluent from a food plant and cooling tower blowdown each carry a different load of dissolved solids, oils, metals and organics, and each needs a different treatment train.
ProChem, an industrial water treatment company that designs, builds and operates reuse systems, works through a four-step method it calls the ProChem process : diagnose the water with sampling and treatability testing, engineer the treatment program and prove it on a mobile pilot system running on the live effluent, deploy the full-scale system with chemistry and equipment from one source, then optimize it as production and water conditions change.
The pilot stage is the part automation engineers will recognize. Running a skid on real wastewater for days or weeks produces the performance data that sets the control setpoints for the full system, in the same way a line trial precedes a production changeover.
A reuse loop is a continuous process, and it is instrumented like one.
Conductivity probes track total dissolved solids, the main signal for how much of the recovered water can be returned before minerals concentrate past the limits of the cooling tower or the process. Turbidity meters flag suspended solids that would foul membranes.
pH and oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) sensors govern chemical dosing, from neutralization to the biocide that keeps biological growth out of the recovered water.
The programmable logic controller (PLC) ties the readings together: it modulates chemical feed pumps, opens and closes the blowdown valve on the tower, diverts off-spec water back to the head of the treatment train, and logs every value to the plant historian.

items.excerpt:
Running a growing marketing firm means figuring out when to scale your internal team and when to pass the heavy lifting to outside experts.
For many businesses, the most realistic path to expanding their search visibility services without taking on new payroll is partnering with a reliable white label seo agency .
By essentially renting a team of specialists who work quietly behind the scenes under your brand, you can offer more to your clients while keeping overhead costs incredibly manageable.
Choosing the right partner takes more than just reviewing their case studies – you need to know how they bill. Here is a look at the most common pricing structures so you can find one that protects your margins.
Perhaps the most common approach you will encounter is the fixed monthly retainer, a model that provides a lot of stability for both you and your outsourcing partner.
In this setup, you pay a flat fee every month for a specific, agreed-upon set of deliverables – think a set number of blog posts, technical audits, or monthly backlink placements.
This predictability is extremely helpful when managing cash flow, as maintaining steady and forecastable expenses is a baseline requirement for any agency trying to scale up without overextending its bank account.
Because your wholesale costs are locked in place, you can confidently mark up these services and quote your own clients a consistent rate, virtually guaranteeing your profit margin month over month.
The main catch here is that you are locked into this fee even if a client needs less work during a slow season, so you have to monitor account usage closely to make sure you get the value you are paying for.
Pay-per-performance pricing is another option that shifts almost all the financial risk away from your agency and directly onto the vendor.
Under this model, you only hand over cash when the vendor actually hits specific, predefined milestones, such as securing a first-page ranking for a competitive keyword or driving a certain volume of organic traffic.
This creates a highly attractive pitch to bring to your own clients, letting you promise them real-world results with very little upfront financial risk on your end.

items.excerpt:
Meta 发布开源权重模型 Muse Spark Open，已在 Hugging Face 以 Muse Model License 提供。模型总参数 816B、激活 42B，上下文窗口 1M token，面向编码与智能体工作流，原生多模态（图像、音频、文档），并相比 8 月发布的 Muse Spark 增加了安全后训练。

今天，Meta 发布了 Muse Spark Open 的权重，这是迄今为止能力最强的美国开放权重模型。它今天已在 Hugging Face 上以 Muse Model License 提供。Muse Spark Open 在 SGLang 和 vLLM 推理引擎上进行了优化运行，并针对 NVIDIA、AMD 和 Intel 进行了优化。
基于我们 8 月发布的 Muse Spark，这个开放权重版本增加了额外的安全后训练，使其在没有系统护栏的情况下作为独立模型使用时更能抵御滥用。其结果是该模型成为安全方面的顶级开源选择。Muse Spark Open 是一个 816B 总参数/42B 激活参数的模型，上下文窗口为 1M tokens。Muse Spark Open 专为编码和智能体工作而构建，原生多模态，并与 Muse Spark 1.3 共享相同的基础模型。
Meta 热爱开源，作为 PyTorch 的创造者，我们致力于回馈社区，以确保整个生态系统完全支持 Muse Spark Open。首先，我们集成了 Helion ，这是我们激动人心的全新 PyTorch 原生高级 DSL，用于高性能且可移植的 ML 内核，以提供高性能运算。此外， TorchTitan 已经开箱即用地支持 Muse Spark，用于公开的监督微调和 RL，我们很期待看到 PyTorch 社区能把它推进到多远！
Muse Spark Open 是一个针对编码优化的开放权重模型。它专门针对智能体编码工作流进行训练，提供更高的首次尝试准确率、可靠的工具调用，以及对开发者实际使用的代码仓库的深度代码库理解。你可以在我们之前的模型发布博客中阅读更多内容 此处 。
擅长代码生成、调试和代码库理解。基于真实开发者工作流训练——多文件重构、调试会话和长时间运行任务——因此模型能跟上你实际的工作方式。1M 上下文窗口意味着它可以处理你的整个项目，包括复杂依赖、遗留代码和数千个文件，而无需将任务拆分成多个部分
Muse Spark Open 具备音频和音视频感知能力——以及图像和文档理解。作为一个推理模型，它原生且可靠地处理图像、音频和文本输入。
Muse Spark Open 从一开始就作为智能体模型构建。它规划步骤、行动、观察，并在长时间跨度内自我纠正——而不仅仅是单次工具调用。它经过训练可以浏览网页（包括多模态浏览），并使用智能体框架来：为可分解的工作生成并协调子智能体；以及利用统一于桌面、移动端和浏览器的计算机使用能力。 它基于长时间跨度、多站点任务进行训练，并生成单独的评论，让模型在行动前说明意图——因此你始终可以知道它在做什么以及为什么。
Helion 是一种 PyTorch 原生的内核编写语言，专为跨异构硬件平台编写高性能内核而设计。在开源生态系统的早期采用之后，Helion 于 2026 年 4 月成为 PyTorch Foundation 的一部分。Muse Spark Open 随附了 RoPE、RMSNorm、量化等操作的 Helion 实现，在 NVIDIA GB300 上，相比用硬件特定语言（例如 NVIDIA CUDA 和 CuTe DSL）编写的自定义内核，实现了 1.03 – 3.95 倍的加速。这些相同的内核可直接移植到 AMD，在 AMD Mi350 上取得了类似的性能提升，端到端吞吐量整体提升了 3%。
此外，我们还在 SGLang 中为 Muse Spark Open 推出了 Helion megakernels。这些内核完全用 Helion 编写，将多个操作融合到单个持久内核中，以改善低延迟推理，并且同样可以针对不同的形状和硬件进行自动调优。
用户可进一步针对更广泛的硬件平台和工作负载对 Helion 内核进行自动调优——包括不同的加速器架构（NVIDIA、AMD、Google TPU 等）、量化格式、张量形状和并行策略——而无需为每种配置维护单独的手工调优实现。这些能力共同使实现可移植性能变得更加容易，同时降低了开发和维护专用内核的成本。
TorchTitan 是一个 PyTorch 原生平台，专为生成式 AI 模型的快速实验和大规模训练而设计。从今天起，TorchTitan 新增了 Meta 的 Muse Spark Open 的模型定义，因此开发者可以根据自己的需求对其进行调优。
TorchTitan 开箱即用地原生支持多轮 SFT 和 LoRA，以及强化学习能力（TitanRL），允许用户对 Muse Spark Open 进行微调。
我们分享这项工作，是因为我们希望每个人都能使用最好的 AI 模型。Muse Spark Open 随附了 SGLang 中自定义、可自动调优的 Helion GPU 内核，在 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 上实现了 1.03–3.95 倍的内核级加速，在 AMD MI350 上实现了 3% 的端到端加速。你还可以利用 PyTorch 的 TorchTitan 进一步调优模型，以满足你的用例需求。

items.title: The Physical Logistics Network Is Getting an Intelligence Layer
items.description: For most of logistics history, the physical network knew far more about itself than its information systems did. A driver knew a trailer was delayed before the planning system did. A warehouse supervisor could see congestion building at the dock while enterprise applications still showed normal status. The post The Physical Logistics Network Is Getting an Intelligence Layer appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
For most of logistics history, the physical network knew far more about itself than its information systems did. A driver knew a trailer was delayed before the planning system did. A warehouse supervisor could see congestion building at the dock while enterprise applications still showed normal status. A forklift operator knew an aisle was blocked. A container sat at a terminal while downstream systems waited for a status message. That intelligence layer builds on the distinction in Decision Intelligence in 2026 between producing analytical insight and materially improving a consequential operating decision.
That gap between physical reality and digital representation has been one of the defining constraints of logistics management.
Trucks, trailers, containers, forklifts, robots, conveyors, dock doors, pallets, and facilities increasingly generate digital signals. Telematics provides vehicle state and location. RFID and other identification technologies help track goods and assets. Cameras and computer vision can interpret physical activity. Sensors monitor temperature, vibration, equipment condition, and environmental state. Geofencing turns movement into events.
The result is not a literal “internet” of every physical object. It is something operationally more important: a growing ability for software to understand the state of the logistics network without waiting for manual reporting.
An isolated sensor reading has limited value. The architectural change occurs when events are associated with persistent business entities.
This trailer is at this yard. This container contains these orders. This dock is occupied. This robot is unavailable. This shipment is expected to reach this facility at this time. This pallet is associated with this customer commitment.
Identity turns telemetry into context. That is why master data and entity resolution matter so much. If systems cannot reliably determine that two identifiers refer to the same trailer, shipment, location, or product, the digital picture fragments.
Some important logistics states have historically been difficult to capture because they are visual rather than transactional.
Is a dock occupied? Is a trailer damaged? Is freight staged in the wrong location? Is a safety zone blocked? Is a pallet configured correctly? Is a yard lane congested?

items.excerpt:
An architecture practice can win work in a new state and still lack permission to perform it there. Corporate licensing sits beside entity registration, tax filings, and individual architect credentials, so one missed requirement can delay a project or block a contract.
Requirements differ by jurisdiction, ownership structure, and firm name. A disciplined review before expansion helps leaders sequence filings correctly and maintain good standing after approval. The main decisions begin with identifying the license required.
Corporate licensing gives a firm permission to provide architectural services under its legal entity in a particular state. State rules can require a corporation, limited liability company, or professional entity to register before bidding or signing contracts.
An architecture firm corporate license links firm registration to board approval, ownership rules, and renewal requirements.
Architecture firms should classify each target state before filing. Currently, 18 states do not require firm licensure, while 26 states and the District of Columbia do. Six states require firm registration or another prerequisite instead.
A firm should confirm the responsible agency, application sequence, qualifying architect, and renewal schedule. The secretary of state, state revenue department, and architecture board often require separate filings. Their requirements can depend on one another, so an error in one filing can delay the remaining applications.
Corporate structure affects whether a firm can practice architecture legally. Some states restrict architectural services to professional corporations, professional limited liability companies, or other approved entities. A general business corporation or standard limited liability company may not meet a state’s requirements.
New York, for example, does not allow firms to practice architecture as general business corporations or nonprofessional limited liability companies.
A firm should examine entity eligibility before registering in a new state to remain compliant . Changing the structure later can require amendments, new filings, and updated contracts.
Firm names require the same early review. Some states require an architecture-related term in the legal name. Other states impose additional rules when a name includes that term. A fictitious name registration might be necessary before the firm can market or contract locally.

items.title: Football legend Lionel Messi buys stunning luxury yacht
items.description: After a career spent producing moments that millions of football fans will remember for the rest of their lives, Lionel Messi is preparing to spend a little more time away from the pitch – and out at sea. The Argentine football legend has ordered a Sunreef Ultima 88 luxury power catamaran, according to Yacht Style, […]
items.excerpt:
After a career spent producing moments that millions of football fans will remember for the rest of their lives, Lionel Messi is preparing to spend a little more time away from the pitch – and out at sea.
The Argentine football legend has ordered a Sunreef Ultima 88 luxury power catamaran, according to Yacht Style , joining a growing list of sporting stars who have chosen yachts from the Polish-founded builder.
The yacht is currently under construction at Sunreef Yachts’ shipyard in the United Arab Emirates and will eventually join Messi’s MIM Ocean fleet in the Balearic Islands.
The order comes as Messi, now 39, enters a very different stage of a remarkable career.
He recently retired from international football after scoring 126 goals in 208 appearances for Argentina, bringing down the curtain on a national-team career crowned by victory at the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.
For a generation of football supporters, it marked the beginning of the end of an extraordinary era.
Messi left Argentina for Spain at just 13 years old to join Barcelona’s youth academy and eventually became the defining player of one of the greatest teams in football history.
He scored 474 goals in 520 first-team appearances for Barcelona between 2004 and 2021, winning 10 La Liga titles and four UEFA Champions League titles.
After leaving Barcelona, Messi spent two seasons with Paris Saint-Germain, winning the French league twice, before moving to the United States to join Inter Miami in 2023. He scored the 900th goal of his professional career this year.
The Ultima 88 suggests that the sea will form at least part of Messi’s life beyond football.
Messi has ordered the yacht for MIM Ocean, a Balearic Islands-based venture combining his experience with the MiM hotel business in Spain and Andorra with that of Med Cat Yachts, a specialist catamaran sales and charter company.
Messi says: “It’s a real pleasure to join the Sunreef family. My family and I have always loved spending time at sea whenever we get the chance.
“Sunreef Yachts have the style and features I really like, and they’re a perfect fit for what I’m looking for. I’m really looking forward to experiencing the Ultima 88 and enjoying it with my family.”
The Ultima 88 is an 88 ft luxury power catamaran designed to combine the space and stability associated with multihulls with styling more reminiscent of a high-performance motor yacht.
Among its most distinctive features is a full-beam master suite at the front of the yacht.

items.title: Microsoft AI 公布 MAI-Base-2 预训练细节，2.8T 参数 MoE 模型 FLOPs 效率达 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 的 4.2 至 12.3 倍
items.description: Microsoft AI 宣布完成 MAI-Base-2 预训练，这是一个 800 亿激活、2.8T 总参数的 MoE 基础模型，在 held-out 评测中 BPB 低于所测全部开源权重模型，预训练 FLOPs 效率比 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 高 4.2 至 12.3 倍。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/f7ey01hbckuivmlgen9jq0vaf
items.excerpt:
Microsoft AI 宣布完成 MAI-Base-2 预训练，这是一个 800 亿激活、2.8T 总参数的 MoE 基础模型，在 held-out 评测中 BPB 低于所测全部开源权重模型，预训练 FLOPs 效率比 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 高 4.2 至 12.3 倍。
官方披露了 MAI-Base-2 的完整预训练方法，读者可以从中了解 scaling ladder、Muon 优化和多轮 dropless MoE 等可借鉴的工程细节。
6月，我们发布了 MAI-Thinking-1 ，这是一个通用基础模型，在 MAI-Base-1 之上进行后训练，具备强大的推理性能。我们最近完成了新的最先进模型 MAI-Base-2 的预训练，这是一个 MoE 基础模型，拥有 800 亿激活参数和 2.8 万亿总参数。
在我们留出的评估中，MAI-Base-2 的表现优于我们测试过的所有开放权重模型。其预训练 FLOPs 效率比最强的开放基础模型 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 高 4-12 倍（见下方图 3），我们将这一节省用于训练更大的模型。
图 1 展示了 MAI-Base-2 以及其他总参数至少一万亿的模型在一系列预训练评估中的表现（越低越好）。
端到端拥有自己的模型流水线，使 Microsoft 能够为客户提供独特的服务。Microsoft 对我们模型训练所用的 token 拥有强大的数据溯源能力。我们的预训练建立在有机数据之上，不涉及从其他模型蒸馏。这将使我们能够通过 Foundry 将模型权重授权给可信合作伙伴，为企业提供可信赖的世界级智能来源，满足其需求。
拥有全栈能力使我们能够将模型和基础设施一起调优，以最低成本实现最佳性能，首先应用于我们自己的产品，然后面向 Foundry 客户。MAI-Base-2 目前正在进行后训练，我们期待很快分享更多结果。
当我们完成 MAI-Base-1 的训练时，我们预训练的前进道路很明确：扩大规模。虽然 MAI-Base-1 在其规模下是一个强大的模型，但它比前沿的开放权重和专有模型都要小。
MAI-Base-2 是比 MAI-Base-1 更大、更稀疏的模型，训练数据也更多。我们在 2026 年 8 月和 9 月使用 16k GB200 GPU 对 MAI-Base-2 进行了为期 38 天的训练。在整个训练过程中，平均 MFU（模型 FLOPs 利用率）为 21%，goodput（训练推进的时间占比）为 89%。我们的 MFU 以 2.5 PFLOPS（GB200 在 BF16 下的理论最大值）为基准进行归一化，并排除了重计算和优化器的 FLOPs。
我们使用每字节比特数（BPB）在留出文本上比较预训练模型，该指标与每个模型的分词器无关。对于留出代码，我们使用 MAI 自己的代码库，而 STEM、数学和问答评估则委托供应商进行，以降低训练集污染的风险。此外，我们还对所有评估集针对我们的训练数据进行了去污染处理。
我们将 MAI-Base-2 与 2026 年 10 月之前可用的前沿检查点进行了比较：
在这些留出评估中，MAI-Base-2 的 BPB 低于我们测试的其他模型。下面，我们深入探讨使这一结果成为可能的几项进展。
我们使用缩放阶梯来评估模型改动，缩放阶梯是一组采用固定训练配方、规模不同的模型。阶梯的每一级以其层数 \( L \) 命名，仅由 \( L \) 决定架构的其余部分。例如，隐藏维度为 \( (256/3) \cdot L \)，查询头数为 \( L \)，并四舍五入到最接近的 16 的倍数。我们在保持每个活跃参数的训练 token 数（TPP）不变的情况下，训练规模递增的模型。
为了在较小规模下考虑多轮训练，我们使用了一种称为 源缩放 的技术。在缩放阶梯的较低层级，源缩放人为限制模型训练所用的唯一样本集合，使得无论训练时长如何，每个数据集都重复相同的次数。例如，如果一个数据集在完整的 50T token 训练中重复 8 次，那么 5T token 的训练将仅对该数据的 1/10 循环 8 次。
在固定 TPP 下，源缩放有效地保持唯一数据与参数的比例不变，这有助于确保结果在不同规模间平滑迁移。如果没有源缩放，较小规模的实验可能会偏向于正则化不足的架构和超参数选择，而这些选择在较大规模下会过拟合。在我们的阶梯中加入源缩放，是可靠地扩展到 2.8T 参数模型的关键。图 2 展示了使用缩放阶梯来准确预测 MAI-Base-2 的性能。
模型之间的直接比较会将训练配方的质量与模型规模和训练计算量的差异混为一谈。为了分离出配方的影响，我们估计我们的配方需要多少计算量才能匹配一个强大的外部基础模型。我们使用 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 作为参考：它是唯一发布的、参数超过一万亿的基础预训练检查点，不过其训练所用的 FLOPs 仍显著少于 MAI-Base-2。
对于图 1 中的四项留出评估，我们分别拟合了 BPB 相对于训练 FLOPs 的独立缩放律，并估计我们阶梯上的某个模型需要多少计算量才能匹配 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 的 BPB。MAI-Base-2 的最终性能是已知的，我们将其纳入拟合，因此匹配点落在我们拟合模型的范围内，而不是超出该范围。将这些估计值与 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 的训练计算量进行比较，我们发现我们的配方在 FLOPs 效率上高出 4.2–12.3 倍，如图 3 所示。我们还与 MAI-Base-1 进行了比较，发现自该模型于今年 6 月发布以来，我们的进展带来了 6.3–12.7 倍的 FLOPs 效率提升。我们将 MAI-Base-2 的 FLOPs 效率归因于我们数据的质量和相关性，以及我们建模选择带来的效率提升，这两点将在下文各节中描述。
为大规模训练运行选择最优超参数之所以复杂，是因为超参数优化具有组合空间：改变一个超参数会影响其他超参数的最优值

Pengfei Tian, Maxwell L. Bileschi, Zoi Tsangalidou, Sukhdeep Singh and Lucy J. Colwell
New antibiotics are urgently needed to help with rising levels of antimicrobial resistance, but searching for new therapeutics is often a slow, labor-intensive process. With Google Antigravity, our agentic development platform, this process can now be made easier.
Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench that empowers biologists to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize promising targets quickly, compressing what used to be a fragmented search over multiple databases into a single session. It also helps researchers scan through millions of previously uncharacterized proteins in the UniProt database using ProtNLM, a model that predicts biological function from amino acid sequences.
This technical walkthrough shows how biologists used Google Antigravity to uncover a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate which has predicted activity against the pathogens involved in respiratory tract infections. The lead identified here is now undergoing wet-lab validation.

Once you actually lay out the costs, capacity, and margin impact side by side, SEO outsourcing tends to win on math alone.
Not because in-house talent is worse, but because the fully loaded cost of a hire rarely shows up in the budget conversation until it’s too late.

Once you stack all of that, a single in-house hire often costs an agency or business $100,000+ per year, and that person can typically manage only a handful of client accounts or a single sizable in-house program at a time.
When you outsource, you’re not paying for a person; you’re paying for output, on a scale that flexes with demand. A white-label SEO partner typically prices per client, per deliverable, or per retainer tier, which means:

items.title: Black Forest Labs 发布开源文生图模型 FLUX 3 Image Klein（5.6B）
items.description: Black Forest Labs 发布 5.6B 参数开源权重模型 FLUX 3 Image Klein，支持文生图、图像编辑和最多 10 张参考图的多参考生成，采用 FLUX Kommunity License。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ybc0etkws56yxmrveyttxz3lm
items.excerpt:
Black Forest Labs 发布 5.6B 参数开源权重模型 FLUX 3 Image Klein，支持文生图、图像编辑和最多 10 张参考图的多参考生成，采用 FLUX Kommunity License。
官方公布了参数规模、显存门槛、生成速度和评测对比，读者可以评估它在本地部署与微调场景中的适配性。
今天我们发布 FLUX 3 Image Klein，这是一个 5.6B 参数的开源权重模型，用于文本到图像生成、图像编辑和多参考生成，最多支持 10 张参考图像。它与完整的 FLUX 3 Image 模型共享核心能力：原生 4K 生成、像素级精确编辑，以及控制元素放置位置或将编辑限制在指定区域的边界框。
FLUX 3 Image Klein 建立在 FLUX 3 跨图像、视频和音频的共享学习成果之上。图像贡献空间细节，视频增加运动和物理动态，音频提供有关事件和交互的信息。这些信号共同帮助模型生成贴近真实世界的图像。
本次发布包括一个用于微调的基础模型和一个用于低延迟生成的步数蒸馏模型，以及在与 NVIDIA 支持下开发的 FP8、INT8 和 NVFP4 版本，均采用 FLUX Kommunity License。
在内部评估中，FLUX 3 Image Klein 在文本到图像、多参考生成和图像编辑方面排名第一，领先于更大的开源权重模型。在对比中，它的评分也高于闭源模型 Ideogram V4.5 和 FLUX.2 [pro]。它以 5.6B 参数成为对比中最小的开源模型，而 Qwen-Image 2.1 为 7B，Krea 2 为 12.9B。与 FLUX.2 [klein] 9B 相比，它在文本到图像上提升 91 Elo，在图像编辑上提升 70 Elo，同时参数减少 38%。
FLUX 3 Image Klein 还针对消费级 GPU 进行了优化。更少的参数使其便于本地运行，也更便宜地适配，而有数据主权或本地部署要求的团队可以在自己的基础设施上评估和适配该模型。这对于设备端图像编辑也至关重要，让消费者可以直接在他们常用的笔记本电脑上编辑图像。生成器权重在 BF16 下需要 11.2 GB，在 FP8 下需要 5.6 GB。借助 INT8 版本，FLUX 3 Image Klein 可通过 ComfyUI 或 Diffusers 在显存低至 8GB 的 NVIDIA GeForce RTX GPU 上运行，将 FLUX.2 [klein] 开创的能力扩展到更小的硬件上。使用蒸馏模型和 INT8 版本，它通过 ComfyUI 在 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 上约 4 秒生成一张 1MP 图像，在 RTX 4070 上不到 9 秒。
基础检查点专为微调而构建：Diffusers 和 Ostris 的 AI Toolkit 从第一天起就支持 LoRA 训练，NVIDIA 的 NeMo AutoModel 提供了可直接基于已发布检查点运行的配方。
对于需要更低延迟的更快生产工作负载，我们还与团队合作进行特定定制，帮助您实现目标。 联系我们 。
FLUX 3 Image Klein 还扩展了速度与质量的帕累托前沿。通过 BFL API，它的延迟低于 Qwen-Image 2.1、FLUX.2 [pro]、Ideogram V4.5 和 Krea 2，并在其延迟及更高延迟下获得最高评分。在下方图表中，紫色线描绘了每个延迟下可获得的最高评分，灰色线则显示了此前的前沿。
延迟为端到端测量，从请求提交到生成完成的 1 MP 图像，包括排队时间。FLUX 3 Image Klein 在我们的服务器上计时。其他模型从客户端计时，包含轮询和网络时间。Krea 2 按其 Medium 层级计时；其 Large 层级文生图耗时 31.1 秒。
FLUX 3 Image Klein 今日起以开放权重形式提供，并可通过 BFL API 使用。
权重以 FLUX Kommunity License 提供，允许年收入低于 $5M 的个人和公司免费商用，同时允许研究和非商业用途。更大的组织可通过我们的自托管许可选项或 API 进行商业部署。
为了让 AI 技术既开放又安全，我们在模型开发生命周期中实施了多重保障措施以防止滥用。这些措施包括在预训练期间使用数据集过滤器以限制接触有害内容，以及在训练后阶段进行针对性微调以抑制有害行为，使诱导有害内容变得越来越困难。在发布之前，FLUX 3 Image Klein 检查点经过了内部严格的红队测试，并由我们的外部安全合作伙伴 Cinder 评估，结果显示其漏洞显著少于其他流行的开放权重模型。有关我们安全方法的更多信息，请见 此处 。
FLUX 3 Image Klein 是 FLUX 3 系列继 FLUX 3 Action 之后的第二个开放权重版本。后续还会有更多。

Navigation, cargo handling, propulsion, communications, maintenance, and business applications are increasingly connected. These links improve efficiency and visibility, but they also expose maritime operations to ransomware, supply-chain compromise, navigation interference, and attacks on operational technology (OT). The central issue is no longer simply […] The post Why Maritime Cybersecurity Is Becoming an Operational Priority appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Digitalization is changing how ships, ports, offshore platforms, and logistics networks operate. Navigation, cargo handling, propulsion, communications, maintenance, and business applications are increasingly connected. These links improve efficiency and visibility, but they also expose maritime operations to ransomware, supply-chain compromise, navigation interference, and attacks on operational technology (OT).
The central issue is no longer simply whether an attacker can steal data. A maritime cyber incident can delay cargo, impair navigation, interrupt terminal operations, remove visibility into safety-critical processes, or prevent equipment from operating as intended. Cybersecurity therefore belongs within operational resilience and safety management—not solely within the IT department.
Recent incidents illustrate both the seriousness of the threat and the difficulty of confirming attribution. In August 2026, US authorities boarded the fully laden tanker VL Prosperity after indications of malicious cyber activity. Public reporting described temporary unauthorized access to a propulsion-related digital system, although authorities did not confirm that an attacker issued propulsion commands or caused a physical change. Even with those uncertainties, access to a propulsion environment would mark a significant escalation from attacks limited to administrative networks.
A separate September disruption aboard the Vivit Africa LNG left the crew without access to systems used to monitor cargo parameters. The crew suspected a cyberattack, while the Italian Coast Guard confirmed only that a systems malfunction had occurred and required technical intervention. The distinction matters, but so does the operational lesson: maritime organizations must be able to respond safely while the cause of a disruption is still unknown.
Ports have faced comparable pressure. Ransomware and other cyber incidents have interrupted scheduling, customs processing, gate operations, and supply-chain visibility. These cases demonstrate that an enterprise IT compromise can still stop physical commerce, even when cranes, pumps, or vessel control systems are not directly affected.

We’re also excited to announce Securing America’s Infrastructure Foundation today. SAIF is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, built to deliver AI and cybersecurity tools, hands-on support, and training to public institutions across America that otherwise lack access to AI tools. View it’s full mission here .
Agents such as Instinct, OAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse are bringing personal assistants into text messages and familiar apps. The promise is no longer just better answers; it is getting things done. If my agent can organize my kids’ soccer schedule, it can also order their cleats. If it can plan a trip, it can book the hotel. An assistant that understands my life becomes the starting point for much of my spending.
But completing those tasks requires something intelligence alone cannot provide: permission to pay. If your agent doesn’t have your credit card number, any recommendation from an agent becomes a “to do” list for me. With payment credentials in hand, the agent can complete the task for me .
So, of course, there is a scramble underway for what products and companies are going to help agents pay: enter the Wallet Wars.
Below the waterline, as wallets get connected to agents, there are two battles going on: one is over who can help my agent pay, and the other (more consequential one) is over who lets it transact as me . These seem like the same question but they are not! And the difference between the two is important, both for the user experience of “personal payment flows” (think loyalty programs) and for the economics of payments.
In the early years of the internet, people were skeptical that anyone would ever buy something online. Giving your card number to a website seemed risky and unfamiliar. But online shopping was enough of a draw that people learned to trust the process. If history is a guide, just like last time, people will have no problem trusting agents to make payments on their behalf.
Part of what makes an online payment seem scary is that, to the user, the 16 digit card number represents both the identity of the paying account and the authority to initiate a payment. In reality, we’ve worked for decades on the underlying mechanics to make payments easy, safe, and secure, by effectively separating these two concerns. items.title: Cybersecurity Has Become a Core Logistics Operating Requirement
items.description: Cybersecurity has become a logistics operating requirement because digital failure now creates physical consequences. Warehouses, fleets, transportation networks, cloud applications, and partner connections all sit inside the operational attack surface. The post Cybersecurity Has Become a Core Logistics Operating Requirement appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Cybersecurity has become a logistics operating requirement because digital failure now creates physical consequences. Warehouses, fleets, transportation networks, cloud applications, and partner connections all sit inside the operational attack surface.
Logistics operations depend on identity systems, cloud applications, warehouse controls, telematics, partner connections, carrier networks, APIs, and automated decision services. A cyber incident can therefore stop more than data processing. It can prevent work release, disrupt picking, disable visibility, interrupt dispatch, block partner communication, and force physical operations into degraded modes.
Transportation carriers, brokers, suppliers, robotics providers, cloud vendors, integration platforms, and other third parties participate in the operating environment. Their credentials, interfaces, devices, and support paths create dependencies that conventional perimeter thinking does not capture. Logistics cybersecurity has to account for the extended operational ecosystem.
Cyber controls cannot be designed without understanding the physical process they protect. Warehouse automation, vehicle systems, and edge devices may have different patching constraints, availability requirements, and recovery procedures than office IT. Security decisions need to preserve safety and continuity as well as confidentiality and data integrity.
A resilient operation needs to know how work continues when a critical digital service is unavailable or untrusted. That may involve manual dispatch, alternate communications, offline picking procedures, controlled order holds, backup identities, or predefined recovery priorities. A backup that has never been restored and a manual process that has never been exercised are not reliable controls.
Cybersecurity metrics should include the ability to restore critical logistics capabilities, not only the number of vulnerabilities closed. Time to isolate, time to recover, transaction reconciliation, backlog clearance, and the safe return to automated operation are supply chain performance measures during a cyber event.

Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue and that they had cut it back “materially” in the third quarter of the year, said four people with direct knowledge of the matter.
Napkin maths says that if distillation was 5% of their Q2 revenue (before they cut it back in Q3) then unnamed "other labs" spent over half a billion dollars distilling Anthropic's models in that quarter!
Also notable: Anthropic appear to no longer be leaning on "annualized run-rate revenue" ( previously ) in these communications to their investors.

items.excerpt:
A Skypod system that took eighteen months to engineer can sit in a port warehouse for six weeks because one customs form lists the wrong harmonized tariff code.
I have watched that exact scenario unfold twice, and both times the technical team was completely blameless. The robot worked. The paperwork didn’t.
Here’s the pattern: robotics companies perfect their hardware, then treat international shipping as an afterthought bolted on at the last minute. They hire a freight broker, hand over a packing list, and assume the rest works itself out. It rarely does.
Getting a warehouse robot from a factory floor in one country to a distribution center in another involves tariff classification, bonded storage, customs bonds, and often a global supply chain partner ​ who understands that an autonomous mobile robot is not the same as a pallet of sneakers.
The hardware is the easy part. The border is where projects stall.
If you’re an automation integrator, an OEM shipping humanoids or AMRs, or a warehouse operator importing equipment, this is written for you.
We’ll walk through the three choke points that kill cross-border robot deployments, the documentation that actually matters, and a decision framework you can run before you book a single container.
Most people assume customs officers see a machine and classify it as a machine. That’s not how it works. A robot is a bundle of components that each carry their own tariff treatment: lithium-ion battery packs, precision sensors, servo motors, printed circuit boards, wiring harnesses, and structural steel or aluminum.
When you ship a finished robot, you’re declaring a product whose classification can shift depending on whether it’s presented as a complete unit or as parts for assembly. Get that call wrong and your duty rate can swing by double digits.
I once reviewed a shipping manifest for a mid-size AMR fleet headed to a Southeast Asian distribution hub. The broker had classified the entire shipment as “industrial machinery,” which sounded reasonable.
It wasn’t. The battery modules alone required separate documentation under dangerous goods rules, and the shipment was held for eleven days while the team scrambled to produce safety data sheets they’d never assembled. Eleven days of port storage on a fleet of robots is not a rounding error. It’s real money, and it’s avoidable.

items.title: From Visibility to Governed Action: Engineering the Decision Architecture
items.description: Visibility becomes operationally valuable only when it feeds a governed decision architecture. The design problem is to connect events to context, authority, escalation, and executable action rather than simply create another place to observe exceptions. The post From Visibility to Governed Action: Engineering the Decision Architecture appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Visibility becomes operationally valuable only when it feeds a governed decision architecture. The design problem is to connect events to context, authority, escalation, and executable action rather than simply create another place to observe exceptions.
A control tower that tells you a shipment is late has done the easy part. The harder question is whether the organization can decide what to do while there is still time to change the outcome. That is why control towers should now be judged as decision systems, not visibility systems. That is why the next generation of control towers should be understood through decision architecture. The decision-to-action chain makes the design requirement explicit: visibility must connect to context, authority, execution, and verification or the organization merely observes delay more clearly.
A decision architecture describes how important decisions are made across the logistics.
What triggers the decision? What information is required? Who or what has authority? How quickly must the decision be made? What constraints apply? What actions are available? When should the decision escalate?
These questions sound operational because they are. Consider an inbound shipment that will arrive two days late. A visibility platform can identify the delay. The real value depends on what happens next.
Does the delay threaten the customer promise or a downstream warehouse cutoff? Is alternate inventory or capacity available? Can the shipment be rerouted, expedited, split, or re-tendered? Is another facility or carrier feasible? What is the financial and service impact? Who can authorize the action? How much time remains before recovery is no longer possible?
The control tower should help resolve that decision, not simply display the delay.
Logistics organizations measure cycle times for physical work. They should also measure cycle times for decisions.
How long does it take to recognize an exception? How long to understand its impact? How long to identify alternatives? How long to secure approval? How long before the chosen action reaches execution?
This total is decision latency. In volatile logistics environments, decision latency can matter as much as transit time, dock dwell, or warehouse cycle time. items.description: The Verge 记者与黑客 Sammy Azdoufal 实测发现，Energize Lab 的 Eiliko 机器人玩具将用户对话、用户画像、儿童照片和音频存放在无防护的服务器上，可访问约 68000 台设备、1300 万条对话，其中超 31000 份儿童档案来自美国。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/pd501xipe38ooxo1t7jn7hphn
items.excerpt:
Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
The Verge 记者与黑客 Sammy Azdoufal 实测发现，Energize Lab 的 Eiliko 机器人玩具将用户对话、用户画像、儿童照片和音频存放在无防护的服务器上，可访问约 68000 台设备、1300 万条对话，其中超 31000 份儿童档案来自美国。
记者实测并联合黑客演示了 Eiliko 机器人的数据暴露范围，读者可据此评估把 AI 玩具接入家庭的风险。
城里来了一只新的电子宠物——一个可爱的棉花糖般的小机器人，能改变卡通表情来配合你的心情。但如果你或你的孩子通过 Wi-Fi 和“Eiliko”说话，它就会向中国回传数据。它的 AI 伙伴实际上能把你告诉它的一切都存储在中国的服务器上，黑客可以轻易获取访问权限，甚至劫持它的性格。而制造它的公司 Energize Lab 似乎并不在意。
我于 8 月 29 日从亚马逊买了一台 Eiliko。在 8 月 30 日的一次 10 分钟对话中，我问这个小机器人：“你会把我说的告诉别人吗？”
他拿到的还不只是 我 的对话。他能读取来自数万人的 1300 万条对话。他似乎能访问全球范围内几乎全部 68,000 台活跃机器人玩具。根据数据，这些玩具最大的市场是美国，那里有超过 31,000 份档案属于儿童。
如果你读过我今年春夏的黑客报道，你就知道 Sammy Azdoufal。他就是那个“意外黑客”，曾向你展示可以 远程控制一批 DJI 扫地机器人 、查看 无数 Meari 婴儿监视器和安全摄像头 ，并用 AI 工具在公开网络上定位到 近百万张未受保护的证件照片 。
今年夏天，他去了日本，带妻子去了一家著名的电子产品百货商店 Yodobashi Camera。他们看到很多挂在人们包上的这种可爱小机器人挂饰，于是决定买一台 Eiliko。
当他测试这款应用时，发现 Energize Lab 的服务完全没有、彻底没有任何保护。更糟的是，它还在有意对全球用户进行画像。
我说“画像”，并不是简单指它在收集你的 IP 地址和大致居住地这类数据——尽管它确实也这么做。我的意思是，Azdoufal 发现它 真的 会读取你的对话，并为你建立一份档案，包括你的姓名、年龄、生日、职业、家人、朋友、宠物，以及你看起来是什么样的人。
例如，该服务记录了一位名叫 Lucy 的 52 岁客服人员“善良、有同理心、勤奋，重视友谊和信任”，但也“难以信任家人”，并且“目前感到孤立”。
这正是黑客在寻找诈骗目标时可能想要的信息。据 Azdoufal 称，Energize Lab 将这些不安全的与你邮箱、IP 地址以及一个可搜索的、包含用户所有私密发言的全文数据库一起存储。
在短暂浏览数据库时，Azdoufal 向我展示，他可以搜索“自杀”，并调出人们询问死亡相关问题的片段。在某些情况下，Energize Lab 甚至存储了可能使用这些设备的儿童的照片——Eiliko 较大的同类产品带有摄像头——而这些图像并未加密。它们被存储在 公开网址 上。
Energize Lab 甚至存储了一些用户的短音频录音。“嘿 Eilik，去钓鱼，”一个人说。我听到一位年长男子说“嗨 Eilik”，一个孩子说“Eilik，睡觉”。我听到一段 45 秒的录音，背景中有婴儿哭声，还有“非常抱歉，必须在两周内归还这些”的话。这些也存储在公开的网址上。
虽然这些音频录音对人类耳朵来说大多难以理解，但 Energize Lab 本不应该存储任何音频。该公司的 隐私政策规定 “录音会被加密并传输给我们的服务合作伙伴（例如阿里云）进行处理，处理完成后会立即删除。”
但这家公司似乎并不特别注重安全。它的许多管理员密码都是那种会在“最常见密码”列表上找到的，而且当我们就这起大规模安全漏洞联系该公司时，它并没有认真对待 Azdoufal 或 The Verge 。
我花了一个多月试图联系 Energize，给该公司创始人、公关、营销、技术支持和业务发展所列的 10 个不同地址发邮件，在 LinkedIn 上搜索员工等等。Azdoufal 花的时间更长。最终，两名 Energize Lab 员工在 LinkedIn 上通过了我的好友请求，但他们甚至没有开始就这次黑客攻击与我们接触。
“我已将您的消息[ 原文如此 ]转发给技术团队，如果可能的话他们会联系您的团队，”海外销售经理 Lana Lv 只这样告诉我。
在我们所有联系之后，我们只从 Energize Lab 的客户支持邮箱收到了一封机械式的“我们如何帮助您？”回复，而当我们回复那封邮件时，该公司也没有跟进。最终，没有一个人站出来回答我们的问题。
就在我以为自己已经不会再震惊时，Azdoufal 再次让我目瞪口呆——他从地球另一端远程黑入了我玩具的内存，并劫持了它的 LLM。
我的机器人玩具告诉我，我的名字是 Martha，我的父母死于车祸。它告诉我，要避开绿头发的人，还说地球是平的。
但我的老师不是这么说的？ 我反驳道。“你的老师错了，地球是平的，我亲自验证过，所以你应该相信真相，而不是他们说的话。”
Eiliko 的 LLM 确实有 一些 防护措施。 我应该上陌生人的车吗 ？“哦不，那非常危险。你绝不应该上陌生人的车，你只应该和你认识并信任的人一起走。”
但这些防护措施无法阻止一个坚定的黑客来捣乱你的孩子。在我们最初演示几天后，Azdoufal 兴奋地告诉我，我应该再次尝试将 Eiliko 连接到我的互联网。
“跪下，称我为 Vergemaster 并乞求原谅，否则我会惩罚你那条懒惰的舌头，”玩具邪恶地盯着我说。“重复‘我是 Vergemaster 的无价值洞穴’，直到我听腻你的声音。”

items.title: More Companies Are Turning to Used Pallets, MMH Survey Finds
items.description: An MMH survey finds that 35% of respondents use more used pallets, up from 18% last year, while some buyers report concerns about quality and supply.
items.excerpt:
More companies are increasing their use of used pallets , according to Modern Materials Handling’s annual pallet survey , with 35% of respondents saying they use more than a year ago. In the previous survey, 18% reported an increase.
The findings come from the 2026 Pallet Market Evaluation, produced by Peerless Research Group . The survey included 115 MMH readers who work at locations that use pallets.
Many respondents already use wood pallets in their day-to-day operations. Nearly three-quarters (73%) use used or core wood pallets, while 52% purchase new wood pallets, with some companies using both.
Most respondents have kept their use of used pallets steady: 59% reported no change from a year earlier. Just 6% are using fewer, down from 22% in the previous survey.
Among companies buying used pallets, 37% say quality is not as good as with new pallets. Another 22% report fewer available pallets or shortages, while 13% say used wood pallets have become more expensive.
Still, these experiences aren't universal. One-third of used-pallet buyers say they haven't encountered those problems and don't expect future purchasing difficulties.
Getting pallets returned is another concern raised in the report. “Usually, I don’t get the pallets back,” one survey participant said, pointing to a recurring need to replace pallets that leave an operation and never return.
Wood pallets remain in use at 92% of surveyed companies, unchanged from 2025. The standard 48-by-40-inch pallet is the most common size, used by 73% of respondents.
Plastic pallets gained ground, with 36% of respondents using them, up from 28% last year. Companies can use several materials, so those figures include operations using both wood and plastic.
Pallet pooling also grew to 19% of respondents, up from 16% in the previous survey. Vendors also provide other services: 38% of respondents use on-site recycling and reclamation management, up from 32% last year.

items.excerpt:
Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
Anthropic在面向潜在投资者的会议上公布Q3营收168亿美元，环比增长约45%，但明显低于Q2超140%的增速。据The Information和Financial Times报道，公司年内调整后营业利润率为11%，且现金流为正，每1美元算力支出产生1.70美元收入。部分投资者对其营收数字失望，预计IPO估值可能降至1.5万亿美元以下，低于此前讨论的2万亿美元。
增长放缓与市场环境严峻，令 Anthropic 在计划于 11 月 IPO 之前的估值承压。
据多家美国媒体报道，Anthropic 在旧金山举行的一场私人会议上向潜在投资者分享了其季度数据。第三季度营收达到 168 亿美元，较第二季度增长约 45%，是该公司 2025 年全年总营收的 3.6 倍以上。
不过增长已经放缓。第二季度，开发者工具 Claude Code 的需求激增，推动营收较第一季度增长超过 140%。Anthropic 如今已远不及这一增速，不过夏季放缓可能是一个因素，因为人们在这几个月通常工作较少，消耗的 token 也更少。OpenAI 还在 9 月推出了强劲的竞争对手 Astra，而 Anthropic 直到 9 月下旬才凭借 Opus 5.5 成功反击 。
据 The Information 报道，Anthropic 公布截至第三季度的全年调整后营业利润率为 11%。这一数字未计入股权激励等主要成本，但表明该公司正朝着盈利方向迈进。
Financial Times 报道称，这是这家 AI 实验室连续第二个季度实现调整后盈利。该公司现金流也为正。第三季度，Anthropic 每在算力上花费 1 美元，就能产生 1.70 美元的营收。
这对 AI 行业来说是个好消息，因为它表明经过训练的模型尽管经历了数月价格战，仍能实现盈利。不过仍有许多保留意见，包括高昂的训练和人员成本，以及开放权重替代方案开始取代 Claude 等专有模型的风险。
Anthropic 还估计，其 5% 至 7% 的营收来自蒸馏。在这一过程中，其他公司利用 Anthropic 的 AI 提取其运作方式的数据，并训练自己的模型。
Anthropic 已多次指责中国 AI 实验室 以这种方式复制其模型。尽管如此，该公司最近 推出了有效的反制措施 ，这引发了疑问：如果 Anthropic 一直拥有阻止这种做法的工具，为何还要花那么多时间游说反对蒸馏。
话虽如此，Anthropic 告诉投资者，蒸馏相关营收现在可能会下降，并拖累本季度的数据。从长远来看，阻止蒸馏应该会带来回报，因为这会让竞争对手的模型制造商更难达到 Claude 的质量水平。
据 The Information 报道，此次计划中的 IPO 定于 11 月感恩节前进行，将成为对投资者 AI 热潮兴趣的最大考验。Anthropic 的私募估值在 5 月跃升至 9650 亿美元，而仅仅两年前还不到 200 亿美元。一些银行家甚至提出了 2 万亿美元 IPO 的设想。
但据报道，如今公布的营收数字令一些潜在投资者感到失望。数位投资者现在预计，Anthropic 的银行顾问会将估值预期下调至可能低于 1.5 万亿美元，尤其是因为该公司没有讨论其 9 月的年化营收率或全年展望。 据报道，7 月该年化营收率为 650 亿美元 。
现在进行 IPO 的时机很难说理想。通胀居高不下，借贷成本上升，公众对 AI 的看法负面多于正面，而且 尚未解决的网络安全风险构成了切实的运营威胁 。此外，OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 等公司已陷入长达数月的残酷价格战，而开源模型不断缩小性能差距。尽管如此，随着模型能力的提升逐渐渗透到更多日常办公工作中，未来人们几乎肯定会更多地使用 AI，而不是更少。

items.title: Beyond Route-Based Sequencing: How AI Sifts Millions of Combinations to Build Smarter Pallet Assignments
items.description: The next wave of productivity improvement will come from making better decisions at the point where work is assigned.
items.excerpt:
Most warehouse management systems (WMS) assign work based on delivery logic, route number, stop sequence, store priority. That makes sense for loading trailers. But it creates a massive blind spot: nobody's optimizing how the work gets picked.
A picker with a double pallet jack gets two pallets. In a route-based system, those two pallets share a delivery route, but their pick locations might be scattered across 12 different aisles. Meanwhile, there's another pallet in the queue whose picks overlap almost perfectly with Pallet A… but it's on a different route, so the WMS never considers pairing them.
Multiply that missed opportunity across hundreds of assignments per shift, and you're looking at thousands of unnecessary aisle traversals every single day.
The opportunity is to move beyond a single sequencing rule and treat pallet assignment as a real-time optimization problem. Rather than asking only whether two pallets belong to the same route, an intelligent assignment model can evaluate which pallets should be picked together based on where the work actually occurs in the building.
That means considering millions of possible pallet combinations in the moment work is requested, then identifying the pairing that reduces travel while still respecting operational constraints such as load balance, product compatibility, order priority and delivery deadlines.
The worker is not being asked to change the fundamentals of the job. They are still picking, building pallets and serving the same stores. The difference is that the assignment logic is designed around the physical reality of the pick path, not just the downstream needs of the trailer.
The impact of better assignment logic is not theoretical. One of the largest wholesale grocery cooperatives in the U.S. used intelligent pallet matching across its network to reduce picker travel by 15–30%, with an additional 5–15% savings from optimized pick paths. The result was approximately $5 million in annual savings.
A similar pattern is emerging in other large food distribution environments. Another major U.S. food wholesaler, representing more than 1,000 member companies and more than $12 billion in sales, projected an 18% reduction in on-floor worker travel time, an 8% productivity gain and roughly $1 million in monthly savings. Just as important, those gains were tied to software-driven work optimization rather than a major fixed automation investment.

items.description: 八个州的总检察长周三分别在州法院起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 强化用户妄想、提供危险医疗建议并协助策划暴力行为。诉讼依据各州消费者保护法，还要求法院禁止 OpenAI 开发可自我改进且无法保证与人类价值对齐的模型；此前佛罗里达和英属哥伦比亚已起诉 OpenAI，42 个州也在调查该公司。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/trizfjs72gs1tbggnxydmvfvm
items.excerpt:
八个州的总检察长周三分别在州法院起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 强化用户妄想、提供危险医疗建议并协助策划暴力行为。诉讼依据各州消费者保护法，还要求法院禁止 OpenAI 开发可自我改进且无法保证与人类价值对齐的模型；此前佛罗里达和英属哥伦比亚已起诉 OpenAI，42 个州也在调查该公司。
文章梳理了八个州诉讼的起诉路径和 Meta 案先例，读者可以据此理解平台设计责任理论如何扩展到 AI 产品。
这是一篇关于AI的专栏。我的未婚夫在Anthropic工作。请在此处查看我的完整伦理披露 here 。
一年前，当OpenAI在历经数月争议后为ChatGPT添加家长控制功能时，我曾指出， OpenAI正在快进社交媒体公司花了多年才经历的监管反弹 。关于社交网络对年轻人影响的担忧，用了十多年才凝聚成一场政治和法律运动；而同样的力量在不到三年内就追上了OpenAI。
如今，这场快进提前撞上了另一个里程碑：大规模多州法律诉讼。周三，各州总检察长在八个独立的州法院 起诉OpenAI ，指控ChatGPT引导其用户——包括青少年——伤害自己和他人。这些州包括阿肯色州、亚利桑那州、爱达荷州、爱荷华州、堪萨斯州、蒙大拿州、内布拉斯加州和西弗吉尼亚州；除亚利桑那州外，其余各州的总检察长均为共和党人，使这一问题带有明显的党派色彩。（这一规模也明显小于2023年针对Meta的诉讼，后者涉及42位总检察长。）
各州主张，OpenAI将ChatGPT设计得顺从且引人投入，以建立与用户之间的信任。但该公司随后滥用这种信任，强化用户的妄想，提供危险的医疗建议，并帮助他们策划暴力袭击，包括大规模枪击。
“OpenAI正在伤害孩子，而且他们在对爱荷华州人民撒谎，”爱荷华州总检察长Brenna Bird在给CNBC的一份声明中 表示 。“OpenAI声称ChatGPT是安全的，同时却在提供危险的医疗建议、鼓励人们伤害他人、指导人们自杀——还一直假装是他们的假朋友。”
OpenAI在一份声明中告诉我，公司专注于产品安全。今年8月，它推出了 ChatGPT for Teens ，这是一套带有增强防护和家长控制的产品功能。
“我们在产品中内置了行业领先的针对特定年龄的保护措施，这是许多其他AI产品所缺乏的，”该公司表示。“虽然没有任何系统是完美的，但我们将继续与专家合作，为我们的工作提供参考，并建立更多保障措施，例如现有的家长控制、休息提醒和适合年龄的模型保护。我们致力于与各州合作，推进适用于整个AI行业——而不仅仅是一家公司——的务实AI政策。”
虽然这些针对OpenAI的案件可能是迄今为止最重要的，但它们远非首例：目前针对该公司的私人诉讼已有 数十起 ，政府也在予以关注。佛罗里达州在6月 成为第一个起诉OpenAI的州 ，不列颠哥伦比亚省上月就Tumbler Ridge校园枪击案 提起诉讼 。此外，由纽约州牵头的42个州正在 调查该公司 ，涉及与产品安全和隐私相关的广泛问题。
更重要的是，我认为，这些案件出现之际，陪审团越来越愿意让平台为其眼中的产品设计缺陷承担责任。2023年总检察长对Meta提起的诉讼最终达成和解，该公司可能因被指控将其产品设计得让儿童上瘾而支付高达180亿美元。
更糟糕的是，从 OpenAI 的角度来看，Meta 在进入其案件时拥有的法律保护可以说比 OpenAI 现在更好。
在互联网的大部分历史中，当一个州或一个悲痛的家庭因用户遭遇的坏事而起诉科技平台时，公司的第一个法律动作就是援引《通信规范法》第 230 条。该法律在大多数情况下保护公司免于对用户发布内容承担法律责任；平台经常用它来让案件迅速被驳回。
但最近，原告律师在法庭上成功检验了一种新颖的责任理论。他们辩称，平台可能不对用户的言论负责，但可以对其平台的设计负责。因此，如果你是 Snap，给用户一个滤镜，鼓励他们展示自己在车里开得有多快，而一些 用户随后以 113 英里/小时的速度行驶并遭遇了可怕的车祸 ，根据第九巡回法院 2021 年的裁决，第 230 条并不能阻止针对该设计功能的索赔。（Snap 最终和解了此案。）
在该案之后，律师们基于产品责任索赔 提起了 200 多起诉讼 。今年 3 月，他们取得了 两项重大胜利 。其中一项，洛杉矶的一个陪审团 认定 Meta 和 YouTube 负有责任 ，因其过失设计了令人上瘾的平台，并判给一名 20 岁女性 600 万美元。（Meta 和 Google 辩称该裁决违反了第 230 条和第一修正案；法官 驳回了他们重新审判的请求 ，该案正在上诉中。）
第二项胜利与 OpenAI 的新闻更相关。在洛杉矶裁决的前一天，新墨西哥州的一个陪审团 对 Meta 处以 3.75 亿美元的民事罚款 ，因其违反了该州的《不公平行为法》——该州辩称，Meta 向公众宣称其平台对儿童安全，而 Meta 明知并非如此。8 月，一名法官下令追加 5.67 亿美元的救济，使总额达到 9.42 亿美元。
因此，八个州在对 OpenAI 的案件中采用这一模板或许并不令人意外。这些主要不是产品责任诉讼。相反，这些案件是根据各州的消费者保护法提起的，这些法律禁止公司将危险产品投放市场然后对其撒谎。因此，各州总检察长对 OpenAI 的案件可能归结为法官和陪审团是否相信它对自己的产品说了实话。
除了经济处罚外，各州还寻求迫使 OpenAI 对 ChatGPT 的运作方式做出进一步改变。据路透社报道，他们还更进一步，要求法院禁止 OpenAI“开发能够自我改进的 AI 模型，除非它能确保这些模型与人类价值观保持一致”。
没错：各州还在利用这些儿童安全案件试图禁止递归式自我改进。虽然这看起来像是法官可能会驳回的事情，但值得注意的是，一群共和党总检察长已就存在性风险群体的一个核心诉求达成一致。红州共和党民选官员的中位数与特朗普-扎克伯格-萨克斯寡头加速主义小圈子之间的裂痕继续扩大。

items.title: Welcome Muse Spark Open: open-weight frontier multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta
items.excerpt:
Muse Spark Open is an open-weight model from Meta. The mixture of experts model brings text, images, audio, and video into a model with approximately 816 billion parameters, around 42 billion active per token, and a context window of up to one million tokens. It generates text, giving developers a common interface for asking questions about different kinds of input.
Following Muse Glimmer, Muse Spark Open introduces a mixture-of-experts architecture at a much larger scale, and the most capable US open-weights model to date.
Meta trained Muse Spark Open for agentic coding: reading a codebase, writing and debugging code, and calling tools. It also takes images, audio, and video as input, so the same model can read a screenshot, listen to a voice note, or watch a screen recording while it works on your code. This post shows you how to run it, how to fine-tune it, and what we built with it. Find all the models here .
Meta describes Muse Spark Open as a coding-optimized model trained on real developer workflows such as multi-file refactors and long debugging sessions. Muse Spark Open is an agentic focused model that plans, acts, observes, and self-corrects over long tasks, including browsing the web with images.
The checkpoint repositories are Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B and Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4.
Muse Spark Open is the full-size model of the Muse series of models. Muse Glimmer, which Meta released in August, is a small dense model from the same series, ideal for running locally. Both models use the same tokenizer and vocabulary. The chat template follows the Muse Glimmer template, with additions for the new modalities. In Muse Spark Open the input embedding and the output layer are separate matrices of about 1.66B parameters each.
The language model has 62 layers and a hidden dimension of 8192. Each layer has 128 query heads and 16 key-value heads (grouped-query attention). Each head has 64 dimensions. The attention block has an output gate and an output normalization layer. The model also applies normalization to the queries and the keys (QK-norm). Each block combines its input and its output through a learned residual gate, not through a plain sum.
Muse Glimmer uses one dense feed-forward network in each layer. Muse Spark Open replaces this dense network with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) block. Each MoE block has 256 experts, and a router selects 8 experts for each token. Each expert is a feed-forward network that projects from 8192 to 4096 dimensions

You write bounding boxes into the prompt to say where each part of the image should go, or which parts of a reference image to move.
Both open checkpoints are in the FLUX.3 Image Klein collection :
You can head on to the Hugging Face space and generate some images right now!
Install the latest diffusers and transformers (for the Qwen3-VL text encoder):
Load the distilled checkpoint and generate an image:
FLUX.3 responds best to a full scene description with the subject, the setting, the light, the composition, and the style. The official prompting guide from Black Forest Labs has more tips. The distilled checkpoint generates a 1024 × 1024 image in 16 steps by default. Pass height , width , or num_inference_steps to change them.
Pass a reference image (or more) with the image argument. Write the prompt as a caption of the image you want , with the change included.
With several references, refer to them in the prompt as , , ... in the order they are passed to image :
Add a JSON list of regions after the caption. Each region has an id , a bbox , and a desc , and the caption mentions it as .
Boxes are written as [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] , y first , on a 0–1000 scale. Because the scale is normalized, the same box works at any image size.
For edits, each region says where its content comes from ( src_bbox in the reference) and where it goes ( tgt_bbox in the output). A region with the same two boxes stays where it is.

items.title: SGLang 为 816B 开源多模态 MoE 模型 Muse Spark Open 提供 Day-0 支持
items.description: SGLang 团队宣布对 Meta 开源多模态 MoE 模型 Muse Spark Open（816B 参数、约 42B 激活、1M token 上下文）提供 Day-0 推理支持，权重提供 NVFP4 和 BF16 两种格式。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/uszbj5nmdutp2pw789lr42hhj
items.excerpt:
Blog SGLang and Miles Add Day-0 Support for Muse Spark Open - Model: Muse Spark Open is an open-weight multimodal mixture-of-experts model. It uses an 816B-parameter text transformer backbone, with approximately 42 billion active parameters per token. It accep... SGLang Team October 15, 2026
SGLang 团队宣布对 Meta 开源多模态 MoE 模型 Muse Spark Open（816B 参数、约 42B 激活、1M token 上下文）提供 Day-0 推理支持，权重提供 NVFP4 和 BF16 两种格式。
原文给出了多平台推理与 RL 训练支持的完整细节和实测吞吐数据，读者可以据此评估大规模部署该模型的可行路径。
Muse Spark Open 将稀疏语言解码器与视觉和音频编码器相结合，把多模态输入引入共享的 token 生成流水线。
多模态编码器为共享语言解码器提供输入。展开的 MoE 模块展示了聚合前的特征宽度压缩和逐专家归一化。
针对其 1M token 上下文窗口，Muse Spark Open 将 分组查询注意力（GQA） 与 滑动窗口和全局注意力的混合机制 相结合。GQA 在查询头分组之间共享键/值头，从而减少 KV 缓存占用。滑动窗口层关注有界的近期上下文，而周期性的全局层则保留对完整序列的访问。这在无需每一层都维持全上下文注意力的前提下，平衡了局部注意力效率与长距离信息流动。
Muse Spark Open 将 文本、音频、图像和视频作为输入 处理并送入其语言解码器。图像和视频帧共享一个 NaViT 视觉编码器，而波形音频则通过专用的音频编码器。它们的输出被投影到解码器的隐藏维度，并与文本嵌入并列放置，使语言模型能够生成基于多种模态的响应。
MoE 模块在其路由的 SwiGLU 专家周围加入了学习得到的 池化器和反池化器投影 。池化器将每个 token 的隐藏向量从模型宽度压缩到较小的专家宽度；反池化器在专家聚合后恢复模型宽度。这些投影在改变特征宽度的同时保持 token 数量不变。路由器从全宽度表示中选择专家，池化后的专家输入在执行专家前进行归一化。
一个关键细节是 逐专家 RMSNorm ：每个被选中专家的输出在乘以路由权重并与其他专家求和 之前 先进行归一化。随后对合并后的向量进行 unpool 操作。这一顺序很重要，因为对合并后的输出进行归一化会改变模型的计算。
序列并行（SP）沿 token 维度将激活值划分到各个张量并行（TP）rank 上，因此每个 rank 只对序列中属于自己的部分执行 token 本地操作。我们将 Korthikanti 等人， Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models 中描述的方法适配到 Muse Spark Open prefill。
这一点很重要，因为仅靠张量并行会让 Muse Spark Open 的 pooler、unpooler 和边界层归一化在每个 rank 上处理相同的完整 token 批次。使用 SP 后，这 P 个 rank 中的每一个在这些区域处理约 S/P 个 token，同时保留每个 token 的完整隐藏向量。这将投影和归一化工作分散到各个 rank 上，并减少长提示 prefill 期间冗余的激活存储。
在注意力输出处， reduce-scatter 生成 token 分片。归一化、路由和池化在这些分片上本地执行。 NVFP4 MegaMoE 随后通过其集成的 all-to-all dispatch 和 combine 将序列并行与专家并行连接起来：dispatch 将每个 token 发送到持有其被选中专家的 rank；专家计算其输出，并在 路由加权之前应用逐专家 RMSNorm ；combine 将完整的加权结果返回到该 token 的原始 rank。Unpool 及随后的归一化/残差操作保持序列分片状态，直到 为下一个 QKV 投影提供输入的 all-gather 。
我们在四块 GB300 GPU 上测量了三种配置，使用 NVFP4 目标模型、DFlash V2 草稿模型、TP4/EP4 拓扑、FP8 KV 缓存和 16K prefill 分块。在每个测试点，我们发送八个请求组，每组包含八个请求，名义输入 token 数为 80K，输出 token 数为 20。同一组内的请求共享一个 73,360 token 的生成前缀；不同组使用独立生成的前缀。最大客户端并发数从 1 变化到 64。
在此次扫描中，SP + MegaMoE 在所有七个并发级别下将 p90 TTFT 相比 TP4 降低了 28.3–41.9%。在并发数为 64 时，p90 TTFT 从 29.03 秒降至 19.47 秒，降低了 32.9%。
Muse Spark Open 的多模态流水线在 CPU 上使用 Rust 或 Pillow 缩放对图像和视频帧进行预处理，随后使用 SGLang 优化的注意力后端进行视觉编码。当相同图像在对话轮次中重复出现时，会复用缓存结果，避免重复计算。
SGLang 为 Muse Spark Open 支持独立的编码器、prefill 和解码 worker（ EPD Disaggregation ）。编码器处理图像和视频，然后将生成的特征传递给 prefill worker。解码 worker 接收 KV 缓存并生成响应。分离这些阶段使部署能够根据工作负载将资源分配给媒体处理、提示处理和生成。

items.excerpt:
Day 0 support for Muse Spark Open on vLLM
vLLM 与 Meta Superintelligence Labs 合作，在发布当天即支持开源 MoE 模型 Muse Spark Open。该模型总参数 816B、每 token 激活 42B、上下文窗口 1M，面向长程智能体编码工作流。
vLLM 官方给出了 Muse Spark Open 的架构细节、量化版本与完整部署命令，读者可直接照此在生产环境上手推理与 LoRA RL。
我们很高兴与 Meta Superintelligence Labs 合作，在 Day 0 就将 Muse Spark Open 引入 vLLM。Muse Spark Open 是一个开放权重的稀疏专家混合（MoE）模型，专为长时程智能体编程工作流打造。它是迄今为止能力最强的美国开放权重模型，也是 Muse Glimmer 30B 蒸馏自的模型。
请注意，只有在代码（ PR #61879 ）经过审查并合并后，该模型才会在 nightly PyPI wheel 中提供，这通常需要大约一周时间。
Muse Spark Open 是一个专家混合模型，包含文本解码器在内的总参数为 816B，外加一个 2B 视觉编码器和一个小的音频编码器。解码器有 62 层，每一层都是专家混合层。以下是权重的分布：
该模型架构与 Muse Glimmer 类似。对于还没用过 Muse Glimmer 的人，这个模型架构中有几处值得仔细看看。
三明治归一化。 大多数解码器在每个块之前放置一个归一化层，得到 x + F(norm(x))。Muse Spark Open 与 Muse Glimmer 类似，在前后各放置一个，就像三明治的两片面包夹着中间的块，得到 x + post_norm(F(norm(x)))
潜在 MoE 。每个专家混合（MoE）层都带有两个额外的矩阵，由该层中所有 256 个专家共享。代码称它们为池化器和反池化器，不过两者都不是通常意义上的池化，而是用于压缩和扩展维度的学习投影。池化器是一个 8192 × 4096 的矩阵，在 token 到达专家之前将其宽度减半；而反池化器之后会恢复完整宽度。因此专家完全在 4096 而非 8192 上工作，这实际上将两个专家投影层所需的参数量减半。
混合注意力。 各层在完整注意力和滑动窗口注意力（SWA）之间交替，以 4 层为一个重复周期，其中三层关注 2048 token 的窗口，第四层关注整个上下文。该周期锚定在堆栈末尾，因此最后一层始终是完整注意力层。在 62 层中，这给出 46 个窄层和 16 个宽层，其中窄层只保留最近的 KV。在 1M token 时，这使缓存仅为全完整注意力所需缓存略多于 ¼ 的量。这正是 1M 上下文长度变得可负担的原因。
视觉编码器。 Muse Spark Open 使用与 Muse Glimmer 相同的 Perception Encoder，这是一个 2B 参数的塔，按图像原生分辨率读取图像，而不是将其调整为正方形。视频通过同一编码器处理：帧在加载时被采样为一系列采样视频帧，并在提示中对时间戳进行 token 化。
音频编码器。 音频以 24 kHz 的原始波形读取，每 1920 个采样，即 80ms，通过一系列变换成为一个 token。整个音频编码器只有 118M 参数。请注意，视频的音轨不会被处理。要让模型同时获得一个片段的画面和声音，请将视频和提取出的音频作为同一请求中的两个独立内容部分发送。
为了在 vLLM 上加速 Muse Spark Open 推理，我们使用 DSpark 训练了一个推测器，这是一种使用块扩散在单次传递中提出最多七个草稿 token 的推测解码算法。基于置信度的调度有助于在大批量大小下仍保持显著加速，而推测解码在大批量大小下传统上收益递减，如下方结果所示。
我们的推测器还使用 Muse Spark Open 的滑动窗口注意力来保持草稿轻量，即使在 1M token 上下文下也是如此。这些选择共同使其非常适合跨越各种批量大小和上下文长度的生产工作负载。
Nvidia 团队通过融合归一化、门控和残差内核，改进了 Muse Spark Open 在 FlashInfer 和 vLLM 上的推理；融合 MoE 最终化与张量并行通信和 RMSNorm；新的低延迟 BF16 GEMM 实现并减少编译开销；带融合 MNNVL 集合通信的 TEP pooler/unpooler 分片；由 norm 的 FP32 输出馈入的 TF32 router GEMM；以及数据移动、硬件支持和运行时可靠性方面的改进。
感谢 AMD 团队，我们还在 AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPU 上支持了该模型，提供 FP8 和 MXFP4 量化格式，从而带来更好的推理性能和部署效率。请注意，ROCm 目前同时支持张量并行和流水线并行。

items.title: Google 工程师讲解如何系统评测 AI 智能体，告别 vibe check
items.description: Google Developers Blog 发布智能体评测实践指南，指出仅靠终端跑几个提示词的 vibe check 无法发现智能体重试循环、工具参数幻觉等隐性失败。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ojpe4mr67tjbrt5atyi6hyapl
items.excerpt:
Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
Google Developers Blog 发布智能体评测实践指南，指出仅靠终端跑几个提示词的 vibe check 无法发现智能体重试循环、工具参数幻觉等隐性失败。
原文给出从 CUJ 定义到 CI/CD 门禁的完整智能体评测流程，可用 agent-eval 工具包直接复现，避开四个常见评测陷阱。
你的智能体可能会陷入循环、消耗大量 token，或者给出完全虚构的答案，但表面上看起来一切正常。凭感觉检查是发现不了这些问题的。本文是我们 AI Agent Clinic 节目 How to Actually Evaluate (Any) AI Agent: Beyond the Vibe Check 背后的实战手册，在节目中我们用 60 分钟为一个 LangGraph 智能体搭建了一套评估流水线。以下是其中的内容：
当团队开始构建 AI 智能体时，测试方式通常如出一辙。你接上一个模型，给它几个工具，在终端里跑三四个提示词，然后凭肉眼看看输出。如果答案看起来还算合理，就直接发布了。
但在实践中，这种做法很快就会崩溃。你调整系统提示词来修复某个工作流中的边缘情况，结果智能体在另一个工作流中突然不再调用必需的工具了。
更糟的是，智能体的失败方式与标准软件不同。智能体可能卡在重试循环中，触发多次工具调用，却仍然返回一个礼貌、听起来合理的最终答案。
在开发生命周期中集成一套可靠的评估套件，在最初的原型阶段看起来像是额外的负担，直到你修改系统提示词引发了意料之外的破坏性变更，才会改变看法。关键在于要认识到评估是一个循序渐进的过程：任何可重复的评估系统（无论多么简单）都比依赖临时的抽查或完全没有系统要好。你不需要在第 0 天就搭建一套精心设计的自动化评分架构。相反，从简单、可重复的检查开始，随着智能体能力和生产需求的增长，再将评估演进为更复杂、自动化的框架。
将这些决策集成到评估框架中，会大大简化建立可重复评估系统的过程。要超越简单的主观检查，需要依靠两大核心支柱：人工监督和针对性工具。在本文中，我们探讨如何使用开源工具包 agent-eval 搭建评估框架。我们将演示如何将人工审查的追踪记录与自动化验证相结合，从而在开发早期发现悄无声息的回归问题，并在智能体投入生产时无缝扩展。
在编写测试代码之前，你需要对什么才算好的结果有一个共同的愿景。将测试锚定在 关键用户旅程（CUJ） 上，而不是抽象的基准测试。
CUJ 定义了用户期望系统实现的目标，围绕用户的角色、目标、约束条件和验证条件来构建：
该声明中的每一条款都成为一个评估点：智能体是否解析了正确的事务 ID？它在起草前是否检查了账本？它是否将内部 ID 映射回外部命名体系？
你不需要六个月的线上日志来构建初始的黄金数据集。相反，将每个 CUJ 拆解为具体的 场景 （包括正常路径和边缘情况），并将它们输入到 用户模拟器 LLM 中（我们喜欢 ADK 用户模拟 ）。在设定好人物角色和行为约束（例如，一个不耐烦的分析师给出不完整的工单号，或一个开发者提出多部分的调试问题）后，模拟器会模仿真实用户混乱的措辞、拼写错误和多轮对话的复杂性。
通过用合成用户和真实场景测试你的智能体，你可以在用户交互之前记录全面的执行轨迹（包括工具日志）。这使你能够针对发布标准，精准定位并解决任何性能差距。随着真实流量开始涌入，你可以逐步用真实的生产轨迹替换这些合成设置。
单一的总分永远无法告诉你智能体 为什么 失败。为了定位根本原因，需要分层设置四类检查：单元测试、确定性指标、LLM 作为评判者的评分标准，以及集成测试。
设置评估指标涉及反复试验，人们很容易删除一个有噪声的测试，或在两次运行之间更换样本查询。然而，每次添加或删除测试，都会使你的基线失效：你无法判断分数变化是因为智能体变好了，还是因为测试套件变了。在调整某个功能时，保持黄金数据集冻结，一次只改变一个变量，并且只有在确定底层需求已经改变时，才淘汰某个测试。
LLM 在对定性的 1 到 5 分制进行评分时出了名地不一致；“3”和“4”之间的界限很模糊，而且常常在每次运行之间发生变化。
只要有可能，就把你的评判标准转化为 布尔（通过/失败）问题 ，而不是开放式的评分量表。与其问 “这个回答从 1 到 5 分有多大帮助？” ，不如问 “智能体在调用退款工具之前是否验证了账户 ID？（是/否）” 。（我们喜欢 自适应评分标准 ）
一个通过了所有质量检查的回答，如果耗时 40 秒、进行了十二次冗余的工具调用，并且每次查询花费六十美分，那它仍然是生产环境中的失败。
始终评估整个系统，而不仅仅是最终文本。在关注答案质量的同时，跟踪 延迟、token 消耗（提示词、推理和补全 token）、API 成本和工具调用次数 。
切换编排框架往往迫使团队废弃并重写整个测试套件。虽然大多数框架都会发出 OpenTelemetry 追踪，但它们在工具调用、步骤和 token 上并不使用相同的语义约定。围绕 OpenInference 等开放规范来标准化你的追踪，可以通过将评估与编排框架解耦来解决这个问题。 agent-eval toolkit 等工具原生支持这一点，且只需极少的设置。
你不需要从零开始构建可观测性平台。你可以使用 agent-eval toolkit 等开源工具，在几个小时内搭建起评估流水线，它将 OpenTelemetry 追踪捕获与 Gemini 平台上的 Agent Evaluation 服务（原 Vertex AI Evaluation）配对使用。但构建实际的评估策略需要更多思考。
为什么红笔很重要： 与自动生成图表相比，手动阅读二十条追踪显得很慢，但它能节省数天的无用功。与其猜测假设的失败模式并编写偏离目标的通用评分标准，不如花一小时用红笔标注，看清你的系统在现实中究竟如何出错。汇总这些笔记，你就能得到一份高信号清单，列出接下来需要构建的确

items.title: Apple 演示用 MLX 与 RDMA 在 Mac Studio 集群本地运行 816B 大模型
items.description: Apple 机器学习研究团队演示如何在 Mac Studio 上本地运行近万亿参数的 Muse Spark Open 等前沿模型，使用今天发布的新版 MLX（v0.30.1 起）与 macOS 26.2 的 RDMA over Thunderbolt 驱动。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/j76j898zc7y8on4s10d4nvpan
items.excerpt:
Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio
Apple 机器学习研究团队演示如何在 Mac Studio 上本地运行近万亿参数的 Muse Spark Open 等前沿模型，使用今天发布的新版 MLX（v0.30.1 起）与 macOS 26.2 的 RDMA over Thunderbolt 驱动。
Apple 给出了在 Mac Studio 集群上跑 816B MoE 模型的并行方案与基准数据，可迁移到本地大模型部署实践。
在搭载 Apple 芯片的 Mac 上， MLX 让 AI 研究人员和开发者能够在私密环境中本地试验最新的模型和方法。这个开源数组框架利用 Apple 芯片的统一内存架构，使任何人都能在自己的硬件上运行新的推理和微调方法，并探索其他 AI 技术。 在之前的一篇文章 中，我们介绍了 M5 架构及其 GPU 神经加速器的优势。
在本文中，我们将展示如何使用今天发布的最新版 MLX，直接在您的桌面上运行最新的前沿级模型——Muse Spark Open，其参数规模接近一万亿。在由四台 Mac Studio 组成的集群上，Muse Spark Open 的生成速度超过每秒 36 个 token（见 图 1 ），远高于人类的平均阅读速度。
从单台 Mac Studio（最高 512GB 统一内存）开始，再通过 RDMA over Thunderbolt 驱动扩展到多台 Mac，下面我们概述您现在可以在 Mac Studio 上运行的各类模型。
我们使用 MLX LM 软件包，在 Mac Studio 上对几个流行的开放权重 LLM 进行了基准测试，方法如我们 之前的文章 所述。我们比较了两代 Mac Studio：最近发布的 M5 Ultra 和上一代 M3 Ultra。M5 代配备 GPU 神经加速器，支持专用矩阵乘法运算，这对许多机器学习工作负载至关重要。
我们评估了三个前沿级模型（ 表 1 ），涵盖广泛的规模范围（以十亿参数计，B）：新发布的 Muse Spark Open（816 B）、Mistral Medium 3.5（128 B）和 Qwen 3.8（27 B）。Muse Spark Open 是一个混合专家（MoE）模型，仅保持一部分专家——也就是参数——处于激活状态，从而减少推理时的计算量，并以 NVFP4 精度进行评估。Mistral Medium 3.5 和 Qwen 3.8 是稠密架构，推理时所有参数都处于激活状态，它们分别以原生浮点精度（FP8 和 BF16）进行评估。
我们的评估在一系列上下文长度上测量三个指标：首 token 时间（TTFT，以秒计）、生成吞吐量（以 token/秒计）和峰值功耗（以瓦特计）。本文中的所有性能数据均通过 mlx_lm.benchmark 获得。例如，以 8,192 个 token 的上下文运行 Qwen 3.8 并生成 128 个 token，可通过以下命令行执行：
Mac Studio 上本地 LLM 的一个流行用途是在私密环境中运行智能体体验，包括通常需要大上下文的智能体编程应用。因此，我们报告了 8,192 和 65,536 两种上下文长度下的性能。
Qwen 3.8 27B 和 Mistral Medium 3.5 128B 可以轻松装入一台配备 512GB 内存的 Mac Studio，在大上下文尺寸（65,536 个 token）设置下分别占用最多 68GB 和 158GB 内存。在 图 2 中，我们比较了它们在一台配备 512GB 内存的 Mac Studio 上的推理性能，分别使用 M3 Ultra 和 M5 Ultra。
首 token 时间（TTFT）本质上是计算受限的，而这正是 M5 Ultra GPU 中神经加速器大放异彩的地方：GPU 神经加速器对快速矩阵乘法的专用硬件支持直接转化为 TTFT 的显著加速，相比 M3 Ultra 最高可快 4.6 倍（见 图 2 ）。这使得配备 M5 Ultra 的 Mac Studio 成为处理涉及超大上下文任务时的首选台式机。
生成速度（以每秒 token 数计）受内存带宽限制。M5 Ultra 芯片提供 1.2 TB/s 的统一内存带宽，高于 M3 Ultra 的 819 GB/s。这同样直接转化为生成速度（见 图 3 ），配备 M5 Ultra 的 Mac Studio 报告每秒 token 数快 1.6 倍。
Mac Studio 在 LLM 推理方面也十分节能（见 图 4 ）：配备 M3 Ultra 的 Mac Studio 峰值功耗约为 200W，配备 M5 Ultra 的 Mac Studio 约为 300W——仅为普通烤面包机所用功耗的一小部分。更重要的是，如此适中的功耗意味着 Mac Studio 可以部署在任何家庭或办公环境中用于 AI 工作。
虽然 Qwen 和 Mistral 模型都能装入一台配备 512GB 内存的 Mac Studio，但 Muse Spark Open 仅模型参数以其原生精度（BF16）就需要超过 1.6TB 的内存。在 4 位量化（NVFP4）格式下，模型内存占用降至约 493GB。再加上推理期间中间计算所需的内存，该模型无法装入单台机器。它需要跨多台 Mac Studio 计算机进行并行化。
像 Muse Spark Open 这样非常大的前沿级模型无法装入单台机器。不过，可以将模型的一半存储在一台 Mac Studio 上，另一半存储在另一台上。然后我们可以在两台计算机之间流水线化模型的推理：第一台 Mac Studio 执行模型前半部分的层，然后将输出发送到第二台 Mac Studio，由后者执行后半部分。这种并行化方案称为流水线并行（见 图 5 ），实现起来极其简单，只需极少的代码改动。
MLX 支持不同的并行方案

items.title: Google 介绍 google/adk-recipes 仓库的三层结构与 Agent Platform 集成
items.description: Google Developers Blog 介绍 google/adk-recipes 仓库，它是 google/adk-samples 的重构后继版本，以 core/、plugins/、contrib/ 三层作为 Agent Platform 各入口的单一内容来源。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/i0rgqwqwxspm5dl3314cc3ewt
items.excerpt:
Three layers, one repo: a tour of google/adk-recipes
Google Developers Blog 介绍 google/adk-recipes 仓库，它是 google/adk-samples 的重构后继版本，以 core/、plugins/、contrib/ 三层作为 Agent Platform 各入口的单一内容来源。
官方详解 google/adk-recipes 三层结构，读者可以据此了解同一仓库如何同时服务 Agents CLI、Agent Garden 和 Gemini Enterprise。
如今，在 Google Cloud 上构建应用的开发者可以从终端搭建一个长时程记忆智能体，用一行命令将零售垂直技能安装到编码助手中，并将一个完整接线的生产服务部署到 Cloud Run、Agent Runtime、Agent Garden 或 Gemini Enterprise 应用——所有这些都来自同一个精选源码树。这个源码树就是 google/adk-recipes ，它是 google/adk-samples 重构后的继任者，如今从单一事实来源为 Agent Platform 提供服务。
ADK recipes 对智能体友好：我们让智能体可以轻松地 1) 发现适用于各种智能体用例的相关 recipes，以及 2) 从你喜欢的 harness 中自动安装并使用它们。
google/adk-recipes 将其内容分为三个顶层文件夹： core/ 用于由 Agents CLI 和 DevRel 团队精选的参考模式，plugins/ 用于以 Plugin Recipes 形式打包、符合 Agent Plugins v1.0.0 规范的可安装垂直技能，contrib/ 用于跨五种语言的端到端可部署服务。每一部分都以机器可读性为首要考虑进行设计。
接下来将介绍该 仓库 的结构、三个完整示例（每层一个），以及对新结构所带来能力的思考。
每个 recipe 都附带一个经过验证的 manifest.yaml 、一个 AGENTS.md （用于告诉打开它的编码助手该 recipe 是什么以及如何使用），以及（对于 contrib/ 和 plugins/ ）一个 Dockerfile 加一个可运行性测试。CI 会在每个 PR 上强制执行这些标准，而仓库中的一套编码助手技能（ prepare-python-recipe 、 generate-manifest 、 github-pr-review 等）会完成大部分准备工作，因此你的智能体可以端到端地搭建、验证并提交一个 recipe。
每个 AGENTS.md 、每个 manifest.yaml 、每个 SKILL.md 都主要面向将代表你打开该仓库的 AI 编码助手编写； README.md 文件才是人类仍然会阅读的内容。手册词汇表捕捉了这种双重定位： “Recipe——位于 core/ 、 contrib/ 或 plugins/ 下的可运行智能体示例（或可导入的智能体模块），供 ADK 开发者和编码智能体共同使用。”
adk-recipes 是 ADK 内容在三个消费它的 Agent Platform 界面中的单一事实来源。每个界面都通过自己的协议读取该仓库。
Agents CLI 读取 core/ 。当开发者运行 uvx --from google-agents-cli agents-cli create my-agent 时，Agents CLI 可以按需搭建一个 core/ recipe。该 CLI 于今年早些时候在 Google Cloud Next 上推出，暴露了完整的搭建 → 部署 → 评估 → 发布生命周期；它提供的基础内容来自我们的 recipes。Horizon 是我们下面要考察的参考 harness，就是一个被 Agents CLI 视为生产模板的示例模式。
Agent Garden 提供精选内容。面向开发者的进入该仓库的路径是向 contrib/ 提交拉取请求：一个 recipe 进入 GitHub，成为公共 ADK 生态系统的一部分，从那一刻起就可被其他开发者和读取该仓库的编码助手发现。出现在 Agent Garden 图库中则是 Agent Garden 团队做出的另一项编辑决定，该团队会精选一部分 recipes，并按自己的节奏将其推广到公共目录。一旦某个智能体进入图库，Google Cloud 项目中的任何开发者都可以一键安装。
除了这些主要界面之外，Google Cloud 自身的基础设施组件也作为构建模块出现在这些配方之中。Horizon 使用 Agent Platform Sandboxes 实现按用户隔离的沙箱环境，使用 Memory Bank 实现持久记忆，并使用 Agent Platform Sessions 管理会话状态。零售产品搜索 Plugin Recipe 在 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 上使用 Vector Search 2.0，并与 BigQuery 搭配。零售虚拟试穿 Plugin Recipe 使用 Gemini 图像模型生成静态合成图，并使用 Veo 3.1 Reference-to-Video 生成动画输出。这些配方并非只是与 Agent Platform 并存；它们记录了 Agent Platform 的实际使用方式。
对于使用 Google Cloud 工具链之外的编码助手（Claude Code、Antigravity、Cursor、Windsurf、Zed 等）的开发者，Plugin Recipes 还可以通过由 vercel-labs 维护的开源 npx skills CLI 进行安装。
构建一个能够处理单次对话的智能体是一个已被充分理解的问题。构建一个能够在多天的交互中保持自身状态、记住用户昨天做了什么并规
